data:36009.title: EPM Power Total
data:36009.summary: Total power measured at the grid connection point, across all three phases. Negative means exporting to the grid.
data:36009.gotcha: This is a 32-bit register and it is LITTLE-endian — low word first, the opposite of every PV register. Decoding it big-endian does not fail loudly; it returns a plausible-looking number in the hundreds of thousands of kW. A live 3-phase site showed exactly that before the fix.
data:36009.check: The total must equal the sum of the three phase registers (36006, 36007, 36008), which are plain 16-bit and never affected by word order. If it does not, the word order is wrong.
sources: V19 36009 description — 'Note: Little Endian Low first, High Latter'

settings:36508.title: Backflow Power
settings:36508.summary: How much power is allowed to flow back to the grid before the EPM starts limiting the inverters.
settings:36508.write_explain: Write the value directly. Zero means no export is allowed at all.
settings:36508.gotcha: The documents disagree on this register's sign — some print it U16 and some S16. A negative value only means anything if the sign is real, so a site that needs a negative backflow setting must be checked against the live reading rather than trusted from the map.
sources: U16/S16 split across the PV documents at 36508

settings:36507.title: CT Ratio
settings:36507.summary: Tells the EPM how big the current transformers (the clamps around the cable that measure current) are.
settings:36507.write_explain: Write the ratio directly. A 200:1 CT is written as 200.
settings:36507.gotcha: Every power and current reading is multiplied by this number. Getting it wrong scales the whole site's readings, and the EPM will limit at the wrong point — but nothing reports an error, because the readings still look like plausible numbers.

settings:36510.title: EPM Mode
settings:36510.summary: Picks how the EPM limits export.
settings:36510.write_explain: Write the mode number directly. One mode runs at a time — this is a selector, not a set of flags.
settings:36510.gotcha: EPM-AX uses this same address (36510) for 'Per-Phase Limiting', which is a plain on/off. Writing an EPM mode number to an AX unit sets something completely different. Always confirm which device is on the other end of the wire before writing here.

settings:36511.title: FailSafe ON/OFF
settings:36511.summary: When on, the inverters shut down if the EPM stops talking to them. Stops a site exporting freely after a comms failure.
settings:36511.write_explain: 0 is OFF, 1 is ON. Default is OFF.
settings:36511.gotcha: EPM-AX reuses this address for a five-value FailSafe mode, and the two apps do not agree on what those five values mean. The simple 0/1 documented here is the EPM meaning only.
